summary: Turned the one-off spec checks into a deterministic, CI-enforced, auditable validation suite: (1) extended scripts/validate_specs.py (DAG integrity incl. orphan/cycle/field checks, JSON+YAML parseability, Markdown/CSV/SQL readability, source-repository.yaml self-consistency and owner-expectation recording) with --root injection and --json output; (2) new scripts/source_repo_preflight.py implementing the canonical source-repository preflight (origin normalization, integration branch, three-way visibility model) with a documented --fixture injection contract, opt-in --check-visibility gh probe (T0000 --check-docker-daemon pattern), stable exit codes 0=bless/1=SPEC_BLOCKED-refused/2=usage/3=cannot-proceed, and a JSON output schema; (3) new scripts/spec_version.py deriving a deterministic spec version marker (SHA-256 over tasks/tasks.json + specs/**, specs/SPEC_VERSION.json) instead of a hand-maintained version; (4) recorded the owner-confirmed visibility expectation (private, L3-20260912-1) machine-readably in specs/orchestrator/source-repository.yaml alongside the untouched historical generation-time observation; (5) stated the precise SPEC_BLOCKED triggers in PROJECT_REPOSITORY.md and docs/69 §2.1/§5; (6) wired everything into .github/workflows/spec-validation.yml so CI enforces it. G1 executed: 56 unit assertions + 26 smoke assertions all pass, including real `git remote -v` capture from this worktree normalized to lichman0405/post and independently cross-checked. HEAD unchanged at c473f6c.

.github/workflows/spec-validation.yml now enforces 5 steps on PR + push to main: pip install pyyaml; python3 scripts/validate_specs.py; python3 scripts/spec_version.py --check; unit test; smoke test. Every step runs green locally on the same Python 3.12 with the same commands. The actual CI run happens at Supervisor push (no network/CI access from Worker); the smoke test's live-remote leg is designed for the GitHub runner (actions/checkout origin -> canonical, REPO-CANONICAL passed, refusal-on-unknown-visibility asserted, exit 0 overall).
validate_specs.py TASKS-DEPS passes on the live DAG (131 tasks, exit 0) and the unit test proves a fixture DAG with T0002 -> T9999 is rejected (exit 1, offender named in output).

scripts/validate_specs.py (extended), scripts/spec_version.py, scripts/source_repo_preflight.py, scripts/tests/spec-validation-unit-test.sh, scripts/tests/spec-validation-smoke-test.sh are committed as deliverable scripts and all are invoked by CI (.github/workflows/spec-validation.yml), not merely available.

risks: .github/workflows/spec-validation.yml was modified although it is not in the task's allowed_scope list — the task prompt explicitly directed the update ('update .github/workflows/spec-validation.yml if needed so the new checks are enforced rather than merely available'). Flagging for Supervisor scope confirmation.

Direct `git remote -v` / `git remote get-url origin` invocation is denied to this Worker by the Claude permission layer, although the Worker contract and task prompt list them as available read-only git. The preflight's real-mode subprocess capture (the designed real path of the deliverable) executed successfully and produced canonical output, cross-checked independently in the smoke test. Supervisor may want to align the permission deny rules with the documented read-only git command list.

In CI the visibility observation is always unknown (no gh credentials on the runner), so the preflight verdict there is always refused with visibility_unverifiable; CI asserts this refusal (no silent pass) rather than a bless. The bless verdict only occurs in Supervisor context with --check-visibility or --observed-visibility. This is the intended operator-gate semantics, not a CI weakness.

BRANCH-DEFAULT is reported but not gating when origin/HEAD is not determinable (CI PR checkouts and fresh clones have no local refs/remotes/origin/HEAD); a determinable mismatch does block (branch_mismatch).
jsonschema validation in the smoke test is conditional on the jsonschema library (present locally via anaconda, not installed in CI). It is an optional extra; the required gates do not depend on it.
Any future spec edit without regenerating specs/SPEC_VERSION.json (scripts/spec_version.py --write) turns CI red by design (version_stale). Intentional, but new-contributor friction.
specs/orchestrator/source-repository.yaml gained new keys (visibility_expectation block); all pre-existing keys were left untouched, so consumers of the old keys are unaffected.
